newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian CPI rises 0.3 pct in Sept qtr.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian CPI rises 0.3 pct in Sept qtr.

text.p: The Australian consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.3 percent in the September quarter for an annual inflation rate of 2.1 percent, the Bureau of Statistics said.
The Treasury's measure of underlying inflation rose 0.5 percent also in the September quarter to stand at 2.4 percent for the year.
In the June quarter, the CPI rose 0.7 percent for an annual inflation rate of 3.1 percent, while underlying inflation rose 0.8 percent for an annual 3.1 percent.
Main features (pct) June qtr/March qtr June qtr/June qtr
Most analysts had expected the June quarter CPI to rise by 0.3 percent for an annual rate of 2.2 percent, and underlying inflation to rise 0.6 percent for an annual 2.5 percent.

The bureau said contributing most to the increase in the quarter CPI were prices of fresh fruit, local government rates and charges, hospital and medical services, urban transport fares, entertainment, vehicle insurance, bread and privately-owned dwelling rents.
Partially offsetting these were falls in mortgage interset charges, prices of petrol, motor vehicles and furniture.
The bureau said the annual September quarter CPI at 2.1 percent was the lowest since September 1994, while the annual underlying rate of 2.4 percent was the lowest since March 1995.
